title: Hero MotoCorp Unveils E20-E85 Ethanol-Compatible Splendor+ And HF Deluxe Ahead Of Nationwide Rollout
text:
Business
Swarajya Staff
Jun 04, 2026 | Updated 09:55 AM GMT+5:30

Hero MotoCorp launched its first flex-fuel motorcycles on Wednesday (3 June), introducing ethanol-compatible versions of its popular Splendor+ and HF Deluxe models.
The new motorcycles can operate on ethanol blends ranging from E20 to E85, marking the country's entry into mass-market flex-fuel mobility in the two-wheeler segment.
The flex-fuel variants have been priced at ₹82,710 for the Splendor+ and ₹72,792 for the HF Deluxe (ex-showroom Delhi).
Both motorcycles will initially launch in Delhi and select regions of Maharashtra from July 2026, followed by a phased nationwide rollout.
The models feature upgraded fuel systems, revised engine control unit calibration and flex-fuel compatible components to handle up to 85 per cent ethanol content.
Union Ministers Nitin Gadkari and Hardeep Singh Puri unveiled the motorcycles in New Delhi, emphasising their role in reducing India's crude oil imports.
The country currently imports nearly 88.5 per cent of its crude oil requirements, making it vulnerable to global price fluctuations.
Minister Puri announced that E85 fuel would be made available at designated retail outlets and priced substantially lower than conventional petrol to drive consumer adoption.
Hero MotoCorp chief executive Harshavardhan Chitale revealed that the motorcycles were developed at the company's Centre for Innovation & Technology in Jaipur with minimal import content.
He indicated that Hero could roll out flex-fuel variants across all 12 of its motorcycle models within two years, depending on E85 fuel availability and pricing.
The manufacturer accounts for nearly 29 per cent of India's two-wheeler market share, selling around one in three motorcycles on Indian roads.
Government estimates suggest that even one per cent adoption of flex-fuel vehicles could generate over four crore litres of additional ethanol demand annually, saving approximately Rs 195 crore in foreign exchange.
India's ethanol blending programme has progressed from just 1.4 per cent in 2014 to 20 per cent today, six years ahead of the original 2030 target, saving Rs 1.84 lakh crore in foreign exchange and delivering Rs 1.58 lakh crore in income to farmers.
